scope: Issue #176 (last of ten): the SubagentStop hand-back check (always-on/subagent-check.mjs), the parent backstop over a per-session subagent ledger (finish-check.mjs subagentProblems + edit-gate.mjs edit-time recording), the shared transcript parser (transcript-files.mjs, extracted from finish-check), the parent claim-downgrade (subagent-claim.mjs), the SubagentStop registration + canary in esk-init.mjs, three shipped agent definitions with skills: frontmatter, the brief template + wording experiment, 13 BDD scenarios (2 in skills-formula + 11 in subagents-apply-skills.feature) + a step file, the test files (transcript-files, subagent-check, subagent-claim + parent-backstop/edit-gate-ledger additions), and ADR-0102. The reviewer confirmed the four questions pass, the grep-test is clean (only session_id payload data, no web/HTTP/DOM), fail-closed routing is sound, transcript parsing has a single owner, the read-only short-circuit runs after the ledger check, the edit-gate records only subagent (not main) edits and only on allow, and every block/flag/downgrade branch is discriminating. It raised 5 findings (2 medium, 3 low), all fixed before this entry.

boundary.evidence: transcript-files is the single transcript parser; subagent-check is the SubagentStop handler; subagent-claim is the parent downgrade. grep clean.

ownership.evidence: finish-check has no leftover transcript parser (imports transcript-files); the ledger has two writers (edit-gate provisional, subagent-check authoritative) reconciled by per-file coverage, not two-copies-in-sync.

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins + sibling imports; no web concerns (grep returned only payload.session_id).

error-handling.evidence: subagent-check: uncaughtException/stdin/try-catch/unreadable-transcript/spawn-failure all route to block (exit 2); writeLedger runs inside block before exit so the parent sees uncovered files even on a refused hand-back. F3 fix: subagent-claim banner is now idempotent. F5 fix: readdirSync is a static import, not a per-call dynamic import.

boundary.evidence: the parent backstop is one function reading the ledger; the edit-gate append sits after every deny path (denied edits are not recorded).

ownership.evidence: F2 fix: coverage is now PER FILE - a file is covered only when some receipt_ok=true entry lists it - so a file an edit-gate entry recorded but the hand-back's narrower receipt never covered stays flagged (was: per-agent union + last-wins, which could over-clear).

dependency.evidence: built-ins; edit-gate records only when an agent id is in the payload and a ledger path resolves (a main-session edit is not recorded).

error-handling.evidence: F4 fix: subProblems is computed before the not-wired allow, so a half-wired parent (explicit ESK_SUBAGENTS_FILE, no record) still backstops. Read-only parent with an uncovered subagent blocks; clean/empty ledger ends at once. An unreadable/malformed ledger is skipped (the subagent's own check is the first line), never a crash.

boundary.evidence: SubagentStop registers subagent-check (not finish-check); the canary runs it on a harmless payload; agent defs carry skills: frontmatter by role.

ownership.evidence: ENFORCE_HOOKS is the single source of the enforcement set; session-setup REQUIRED_HOOKS mirrors it (updated to subagent-check).

error-handling.evidence: the enforcement canary's harmless subagent-check payload (no transcript) allows (exit 0); ADR-0102 now discloses that no-transcript escape, the named-skill scoping and its fail-open, the per-file coverage, and the agent-id dependence of the backstop.

boundary.evidence: 13 scenarios drive the real scripts; scenario 1 asserts the router-required skills for a .py module are in the implementer frontmatter (not vacuous).

ownership.evidence: the step file is self-contained; no step-text collisions (clean bdd-run of 95).

error-handling.evidence: new discriminating tests pin the F1 scoped-named-skill (no over-block), the F2 per-file over-clear (a.py flagged, b.py cleared), and the F3 idempotent banner. 63 affected unit tests + 95 BDD scenarios green.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED (substring + no word boundary, over the whole first user turn): a first turn containing the directive's full skill list would mark every skill 'named' and over-block; short folder names could match incidental prose. Only the fail-open miss direction was disclosed.
findings.resolution: fixed: the match is scoped to the brief's '## Skills' block when the template header is present (else the whole brief), and uses word boundaries for folder names and aliases; ADR-0102 now discloses the over-block direction. A discriminating test asserts a skill mentioned outside the Skills block is not treated as named.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: per-agent union of files with last-entry receipt_ok could CLEAR a file the hand-back's (narrower) receipt never covered, if an edit-gate entry recorded a file the hand-back's CHANGED set missed (e.g. a malformed transcript line skipped by the parser). The over-clear direction was undisclosed.
findings.resolution: fixed: coverage is now PER FILE - a file is flagged unless some receipt_ok=true entry actually lists it. A discriminating test covers b.py via the hand-back and leaves a.py (edit-gate only) flagged.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: the phrase-tagging was idempotent but the banner was prepended unconditionally, contradicting the 'idempotent' comment; re-feeding stacked banners.
findings.resolution: fixed: the banner is skipped when the report already starts with it; a discriminating test asserts a double-downgrade yields one banner.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: the not-wired allow preceded subagentProblems(), so a half-wired parent (explicit ESK_SUBAGENTS_FILE, no record, enforcement off) allowed without reading the ledger.
findings.resolution: fixed: subProblems is computed first and the not-wired allow requires it to be empty.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: VERIFY_PHRASES tags negated claims ('did not verify') - over-match in the SAFE direction; and subagent-check used a per-call dynamic import for readdirSync while all other fs is static.
findings.resolution: readdirSync made a static import; the negated-claim tagging left as-is (safe direction - it never presents an unproven claim as fact).
